issues.description: The solution implementation of PersonService.addChild declares the parameters in the reversed order compared to the problem specification and the template usage. The problem statement and template expect addChild(Person person, Person child) (parent first, child second). In the solution the method is declared as addChild(Person child, Person person). Because Java matches arguments positionally, PersonResource invokes personService.addChild(person, persistedChild) (parent, child) which will be passed to the solution method as (child=parent, person=child) and thus the internal checks and updates operate on the wrong objects. This is a structural mismatch between specification/template and the solution and leads to incorrect runtime behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the specification and template by changing the solution method signature to addChild(Person person, Person child) and implement the logic accordingly: check child.getParents() for the child argument, add the child to person's children, and save the person. Alternatively, change all call sites (PersonResource) to match the solution's parameter order, but the preferred fix is to match the problem statement/template signature so behavior is consistent.

issues.description: The method PersonService.addChild uses different parameter ordering/names between the problem statement/template and the solution. The problem statement and template define addChild(Person person, Person child) (first parameter = parent, second = child), and PersonResource calls personService.addChild(person, persistedChild) accordingly. In the solution, the implemented signature is addChild(Person child, Person person) (parameters reversed), which preserves functionality (both parameters are Person) but changes the parameter identifiers and order. This creates a mapping confusion for students who read the problem/template and expect the first parameter to represent the parent (named 'person'), while the solution's implementation swaps these names.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the parameter ordering and names for addChild across all artifacts. Rename or reorder the solution method to match the problem/template signature: public Person addChild(Person person, Person child) { ... } (first parameter = parent, second = child), and update parameter variable names inside the method accordingly. Alternatively, update the problem statement and template to explicitly document the reversed parameter order if that was intentional.
